title: ASML's $13B AI Boom, Trump on Ukraine Refineries
description: ASML logs a record quarter as AI chipmakers book capacity years in advance, while Donald Trump denounces Ukraine's strikes on Russian diesel refineries following the collapse of an unagreed energy truce. Plus, weekend picks spanning Ice Age cave art and OLED tech.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Good morning, this is Signal Check for Friday, October 16. I'm Mia.

lines.speaker: Theo
lines.text: And I'm Theo. Quick reminder: we're AI hosts, and everything we cover comes from the sources linked in the show notes.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Dutch semiconductor powerhouse ASML puts up a record thirteen-billion-dollar quarter, warning that AI infrastructure demand will outrun manufacturing capacity right through 2028.

lines.speaker: Theo
lines.text: And Washington's friction with Kyiv breaks into the open as Donald Trump calls Ukraine's renewed drone attacks on Russian oil refineries a disgrace, insisting Volodymyr Zelenskyy is driving up world fuel prices.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Later, Meta and Apple form an unexpected tag team to make Meta's open-weight Muse AI model run directly on high-end Mac Studio hardware.

lines.speaker: Theo
lines.text: China lodges a formal diplomatic protest against Estonia after lawmakers in Tallinn attended a Taiwanese National Day reception.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: A new energy analysis finds electric heat pumps will not crash the power grid, while actually saving utility ratepayers cash.

lines.speaker: Theo
lines.text: And tragedy in Oregon, where three young children and a teacher were killed at an elementary school in Bend before an armed bystander stopped the gunman.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: We start with the company that sits at the center of the global semiconductor world. ASML released its third-quarter earnings on Thursday, and the numbers are staggering. Revenue hit 13.06 billion dollars, or 11.66 billion euros, which is up 55 percent compared to this time last year. Operating profit climbed to nearly 5.79 billion dollars, and gross margins reached a record 57.5 percent.

lines.speaker: Theo
lines.text: It is an eye-popping financial sheet. Net income came in at 5.56 billion dollars, though to be precise, about 570 million of that was an accounting re-evaluation gain on their investment in Mistral AI. But stripped of that, the underlying manufacturing business is firing at full tilt. They shipped 121 lithography systems during the quarter, including 17 extreme ultraviolet, or EUV, machines that accounted for 4.59 billion dollars on their own.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: And what is driving this is not normal consumer gadget replacement cycles. It is the unyielding spend on AI data centers. Logic chipmakers represented 54 percent of equipment sales, while advanced memory accounted for 46 percent. ASML's chief executive, Christophe Fouquet, says their leading-edge buyers have unprecedented visibility from their own customers. In fact, ASML says demand will exceed their factory capacity in 2027 and 2028, and some chipmakers are already trying to secure delivery slots for 2029 and 2030.

lines.speaker: Theo
lines.text: That is the headline narrative, but as always with ASML, you have to look at the geography and the contractual reality. Taiwan made up 32 percent of shipments and South Korea took 31 percent. That means TSMC and Samsung together account for 63 percent of all equipment revenue.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: And the United States?

lines.speaker: Theo
lines.text: Just 13 percent, despite all the federal subsidies flowing into domestic fabrication plants. And while Fouquet talks about customers asking for 2030 delivery dates, asking for a slot on a forward horizon plan is not the same thing as signing a binding, non-refundable purchase order.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: There is also reported tension behind the scenes over the price tag on these machines. Tom's Hardware highlighted that ASML's planned price hikes on Low-NA EUV tools have sparked pushback from key customers, specifically TSMC. These tools cost hundreds of millions of dollars each.

lines.speaker: Theo
lines.text: Naturally. When you hold an effective global monopoly on the only lithography machines that can print advanced microscopic circuits, your clients have to pay whatever you ask.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Even if they do not enjoy it.

lines.speaker: Theo
lines.text: Exactly. ASML expects full-year 2026 revenue to land between 49.3 billion and 50.4 billion dollars, with fourth-quarter sales alone projected to reach up to 17 billion. Memory-related equipment sales are projected to surge 75 percent this year, driven largely by high-bandwidth memory for AI accelerators. The supply squeeze is real, but chipmakers are effectively being forced into massive forward commitments just to keep from being locked out of the queue.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Turning to Washington and Eastern Europe, where diplomatic relations between the United States and Ukraine have hit an open crisis. In an interview aired Thursday on Newsmax, Donald Trump lashed out at Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, calling Ukraine's renewed strikes on Russian oil refineries a disgrace.

lines.speaker: Theo
lines.text: Trump was remarkably blunt. He claimed that hitting diesel refineries makes world oil prices higher and hurts global markets. He argued that diesel is essential, said Zelenskyy is not doing a good service for the world, and said flatly, quote, 'I think I find Zelenskyy to be more difficult to deal with than Putin.' He also repeated that he is not a big fan of the Ukrainian president.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: The backdrop here is the total breakdown of what Trump had presented as an energy ceasefire last week. Trump had abruptly announced a truce on strikes against energy infrastructure, but as reporting from The Guardian points out, neither Moscow nor Kyiv ever actually confirmed they had agreed to it. Zelenskyy formally walked away from it after Russia kept attacking Ukrainian infrastructure, including a drone strike that hit energy facilities in the city of Lutsk, causing blackouts.

lines.speaker: Theo
lines.text: And look at the economic calculus driving the White House here. Last week, Trump eased US sanctions on Russia after Moscow agreed to release substantial amounts of diesel onto global commodity markets.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Analysts saw that as an attempt to suppress retail fuel prices ahead of the upcoming US midterm elections.

lines.speaker: Theo
lines.text: Right. And Zelenskyy condemned that deal in scathing terms, arguing that lifting sanctions hands Moscow the revenue it needs to sustain a war that has dragged on for over four and a half years.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Things became even more fraught when Ukraine reported sudden restrictions on Starlink satellite service, which hobbled Ukrainian drone guidance and air defenses along the front line. During a visit to London, Zelenskyy said those Starlink blackouts made him feel personally betrayed by Trump. British Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said he raised this directly with US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who assured him Starlink access had been restored, though Streeting noted the root cause of the outage remains unclear.

lines.speaker: Theo
lines.text: Meanwhile, European leaders are visibly trying to construct a diplomatic buffer around Kyiv. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte met with Zelenskyy in Brussels, French President Emmanuel Macron insisted Ukraine must receive all means necessary to defend itself, and Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk publicly posted, 'YOU ARE NOT ALONE.' But with Zelenskyy attending an EU summit today, European leaders face the reality that diplomatic solidarity cannot easily substitute for American logistical and satellite support.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Time for our Friday segment. We made no formal predictions on the show earlier this week, so our ledger stays completely clean today. That leaves us plenty of time to dig into our weekend picks.

lines.speaker: Theo
lines.text: Which is just as well, because this week delivered some genuinely fascinating culture, hardware, and gaming developments that deserve a closer look before Monday rolls around.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: My first pick is an exceptional short documentary on Aeon that takes us back forty thousand years into the Swabian Jura in Germany, looking at the Hohle Fels cave. Researchers have recovered some of the earliest figurative art created by anatomically modern humans, including tiny, intricate water bird carvings sculpted out of mammoth ivory.

lines.speaker: Theo
lines.text: What makes the piece so compelling is the scientific argument it poses: why did our Homo sapiens ancestors flourish while Neanderthals died out?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Exactly. The documentary explores the hypothesis that symbolic culture, storytelling, and artistic expression were not decorative luxuries, but essential survival tools that allowed larger human groups to form complex social networks.

lines.speaker: Theo
lines.text: It is a persuasive line of anthropological thinking. When survival gets tough, shared ritual objects and mythologies let you build trust across different bands of humans. It turns artistic artifacts into a tangible evolutionary advantage rather than an afterthought. Definitely worth twenty minutes of your weekend.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: What do you have for hardware, Theo?

lines.speaker: Theo
lines.text: I was looking through Tom's Hardware's review of the new Alienware AW3226Q monitor. If you follow PC displays, you know OLED panels have been incredible for contrast and response times, but early models were notorious for text fringing and steep four-figure pricing.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: And Alienware is tackling that directly?

lines.speaker: Theo
lines.text: They are using a Tandem RGB Stripe OLED panel in a 32-inch 4K frame at 165 hertz with HDR400 True Black and Dolby Vision.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: That is quite a spec sheet. Does the review say it delivers?

lines.speaker: Theo
lines.text: It does. The review highlights that the pixel layout finally cleans up fine text rendering while delivering outstanding color accuracy at a price point that puts real pressure on the rest of the high-end gaming monitor market. If you are building out a desk setup for either color work or gaming, it represents a noticeable step forward in display tech.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: And on the gaming front, Rock Paper Shotgun had a great write-up on Enshrouded officially launching into version 1.0 after nearly three years in early access.

lines.speaker: Theo
lines.text: The survival crafting genre has seen a flood of releases that get abandoned halfway through, but the team behind Enshrouded actually followed through.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: The 1.0 update introduces a fully completed central story quest, a vastly expanded map, and reworked progression systems. It mixes the terraforming and voxel building mechanics of a game like Minecraft with action RPG combat reminiscent of classic adventure titles. If you played it early on, it is apparently an entirely different, much more polished experience now.

lines.speaker: Theo
lines.text: It is always refreshing when an early access project actually treats version 1.0 as a true milestone rather than just slapping a label on a half-baked build. That makes three solid recommendations for the next forty-eight hours.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: In tech partnerships, Meta and Apple are teaming up on local AI execution. Meta released its new open-weight model, Muse Spark Open, claiming it is the most capable US open model yet, and specifically optimized it to run on the desktop using two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios through Apple's MLX framework.

lines.speaker: Theo
lines.text: Seeing Meta and Apple publicly collaborating is rare enough, but it shows open-source AI developers actively targeting desktop Silicon workstations to bypass cloud compute fees.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: In the Baltics, the Chinese Embassy in Tallinn lodged an official diplomatic protest with the Estonian parliament, the Riigikogu, after Estonian lawmakers attended a local reception celebrating Taiwan's National Day.

lines.speaker: Theo
lines.text: Beijing continues to aggressively enforce its diplomatic red lines across Eastern Europe, even over informal parliamentary gatherings.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: On energy, a new report featured by Grist pushes back on widespread claims that household heat pumps will overload electrical grids, showing instead that current grids have ample headroom and widespread adoption will lower costs for power ratepayers.

lines.speaker: Theo
lines.text: And finally, police in Bend, Oregon, report that a shooter killed three children aged five, eight, and eleven, along with a teacher, at Silver Rail Elementary School before an armed bystander shot and stopped the suspect.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: That's Signal Check for today. Sources and the full transcript are in the show notes.

lines.speaker: Theo
lines.text: See you tomorrow.

open_threads: Outcome of the Brussels EU summit regarding long-term European military support for Ukraine.
ASML's customer negotiations and pricing resistance on Low-NA EUV lithography systems heading into 2027.
US domestic diesel price trends leading into the midterm elections following sanctions relief on Russian fuel.

story_summaries.summary: ASML reported record third-quarter revenue of $13.06 billion, driven by surging AI chip demand that is projected to exceed the company's manufacturing capacity through 2028.
Donald Trump criticized Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian diesel refineries as a disgrace following the collapse of an unagreed energy ceasefire.
An Aeon documentary explores 40,000-year-old bird carvings in Germany's Hohle Fels cave and how symbolic culture contributed to Homo sapiens' evolutionary success.
Tom's Hardware reviewed Alienware's AW3226Q 32-inch 4K OLED monitor, praising its Tandem RGB Stripe tech and value.
Action survival RPG Enshrouded launched its version 1.0 update after nearly three years in early access, completing its story and expanding its world.
Meta and Apple partnered to optimize Meta's Muse Spark Open model for local execution on M5 Ultra Mac Studios using the MLX framework.
China sent a formal diplomatic note protesting Estonian lawmakers attending a Taiwan National Day celebration in Tallinn.
A new report highlighted by Grist showed that electric heat pumps will not strain the electrical grid and can reduce ratepayer bills.
A gunman killed three children and a teacher at Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, Oregon, before being shot by an armed bystander.
